Ser vs. Estar (Identity vs. State)
Choosing between the two 'to be' verbs
ser (essence, identity, origin, time) | estar (location, temporary state, emotion)
Soy de Madrid y soy estudiante.
soy deh mah-DREED y soy ehs-too-DYAHN-teh
I am from Madrid and I am a student.
Estoy en casa y estoy muy feliz.
ehs-TOY ehn KAH-sah y ehs-TOY mwee feh-LEES
I am at home and I am very happy.
ser vs estar
Remember DOCTOR (Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time, Origin, Relationship) for ser, and PLACE (Position, Location, Action, Condition, Emotion) for estar.
Present Tense: Regular -ar / -er / -ir
Expressing habitual actions and current facts
Stem + -o, -as/-es, -a/-e, -amos/-emos/-imos, -an/-en
Yo hablo español todos los días.
yoh AH-bloh ehs-pah-NYOHL TOH-dohs lohs DEE-ahs
I speak Spanish every day.
Ellos comen pan y viven en Valencia.
EH-yohs KOH-mehn pahn y BEE-behn ehn bah-LEHN-syah
They eat bread and live in Valencia.
Gender & Definite/Indefinite Articles
Matching el/la/los/las and un/una with noun gender
el / un (masculine) | la / una (feminine) | -s / -es (plural)
El libro está sobre la mesa.
ehl LEE-broh ehs-TAH SOH-breh lah MEH-sah
The book is on the table.
Tengo una hermana y dos hermanos.
TEHN-goh OO-nah ehr-MAH-nah y dohs ehr-MAH-nohs
I have a sister and two brothers.
Adjective Agreement
Adjectives match the noun in gender and number
Noun + Adjective (-o/-a, -os/-as, or invariant -e/-consonant)
La casa blanca es muy bonita.
lah KAH-sah BLAHN-kah ehs mwee boh-NEE-tah
The white house is very pretty.
Los coches nuevos son rápidos.
lohs KOH-chehs NWEH-bohs sohn RRAH-pee-dohs
The new cars are fast.
Gustar (Expressing Likes)
Something is pleasing to someone (indirect object + gustar)
(A + person) + me/te/le/nos/les + gusta (singular/infinitive) / gustan (plural)
Me gusta mucho la música española.
meh GOOS-tah MOO-choh lah MOO-see-kah ehs-pah-NYOH-lah
I really like Spanish music.
¿Te gustan los libros de historia?
teh GOOS-tahn lohs LEE-brohs deh ees-TOH-ryah
Do you like history books?
gustar vs querer
Gustar means 'to please' (subject is the thing liked). Querer means 'to want' or 'to love' (subject is the person).
Hay (There is / There are)
Stating the existence of something
hay + indefinite noun / number (invariant for singular & plural)
Hay un restaurante cerca de aquí.
ay oon rehs-tow-RAHN-teh SEHR-kah deh ah-KEE
There is a restaurant near here.
Hay muchas personas en la calle.
ay MOO-chahs pehr-SOH-nahs ehn lah KAH-yeh
There are many people in the street.
hay vs está
Use hay for non-specific existence ('there is a cafe'). Use está/están for specific, known locations ('the cafe is on the corner').
Ir + a + Infinitive (Near Future)
Talking about plans and things going to happen soon
ir (present) + a + infinitive verb
Mañana voy a estudiar español.
mah-NYAH-nah boy ah ehs-too-DYAHR ehs-pah-NYOHL
Tomorrow I am going to study Spanish.
Vamos a comer en ese restaurante.
BAH-mohs ah koh-MEHR ehn EH-seh rehs-tow-RAHN-teh
We are going to eat at that restaurant.
Tener que + Infinitive (Obligation)
Expressing what someone has to do
tener (conjugated) + que + infinitive
Tengo que trabajar hoy.
TEHN-goh keh trah-bah-HAHR oy
I have to work today.
Tienes que leer este libro.
TYEH-nehs keh leh-EHR EHS-teh LEE-broh
You have to read this book.
